Icarus Dive applies a slow on enemies. Don't just use it as a gap closer and cancel before you land on an enemy, bathe them in the fire debuff first.

You can pick things up mid-Dive. You can use this to snatch runes and carry on with your business. To time it properly, just cast the Dive at the X:00 mark. To position it properly, just hover over the spell and you can see the green circle cast range.
You can begin channeling an Outpost or Watcher mid-Dive. Just be aware that if you cancel the Dive, you cancel the channel. So ideally you want to start the channeling from the tip of your Dive.
You can cast spells and items while flying in Icarus Dive. This is important when trying to catch enemies, lay some damage on them with items or Fire Spirits, and then safely retreat in the Dive.
notes: You can begin channeling a TP while Diving, but canceling the Dive will cancel the TP, so you'll return to your starting point before the TP finishes.
You can begin channeling a Meteor Hammer mid-Dive.

Shiva's Guard takes a little longer than ~2 seconds to fully expand and will affect any units it makes contact with while expanding. Don't jump into an Icarus Dive the moment you cast it or you'll waste a ton of the Arctic Blast radius.

tips.text: Don't rapid fire your Fire Spirits on single targets. The debuff lasts for a few seconds and the damage from multiple Spirits do not stack, they just refresh the debuff. Enemies are much more wary of a Phoenix who still has a Spirit circling around them. Space out Launches, even if you don't land them.
Fire Spirits briefly provide ground vision wherever they land. Useful for scouting Rosh or counterwarding cliffs.
Sun Ray provides vision over the 'projectile,' allowing you to check the Rosh pit or scout in trees with the beam of fire.
Sun Ray does not work on Rosh.
You can cast all your spells while Sun Ray is out.
notes: If you have Agh's Shard, always try to cast Sun Ray before activating Supernova. Supernova refreshes cooldowns on cast, not when the spell ends. So if you Sun Ray mid-Supernova, you'll respawn with Sun Ray on cooldown.

tips.text: You can cast items while in Sun Ray. In fact, you don't even have to turn your hero to target items if you cast it during Sun Ray.
notes: If you begin channeling a TP while moving in Sun Ray, you will continue moving during the channel. Escape enemies by TPing over cliffs (including the unpathable edges of the map).

tips.text: Try to hit enemies with Fire Spirits to slow their attack speed before going into Supernova.

Try to find cliffs to Supernova onto if the positioning is convenient. Not only are you giving your team vision and potentially evading enemy vision, but heroes will also uphill miss while attacking your Egg as well.
notes: Activating Supernova destroys trees in a huge radius so you can't easily hide the Egg in trees.

tips.text: Allies can fog your Supernova Egg with vision blockers like the front of Drow Ranger's Agh's Shard Glacier or Nature's Prophet's Sprout trees.
Supernova forces the entire map to day time during its duration. It'll even override Night Stalker's Dark Ascension and Luna's Eclipse that typically force night time.
Unlike most other ward units, Supernova doesn't take damage from towers or even the enemy fountain.
For some reason, you can remove Bane's Nightmare off allies while in your Supernova egg if they're in your attack range.
Allies can deny the Supernova Egg once it's under 50%.
If an ally dies in an Agh's Scepter Supernova, it counts as a deny by Phoenix.
Self-damage does not proc Aeon Disk, so you don't have to worry about popping your own Disk from casting any of your spells.

counters.text: Icarus Dive can be canceled with stuns, cyclones, hexes, sleeps, fears, and spells/items causing forced movement or knockback. Phoenixes will often pull some downright stupid Dives because they assume they'll be able to complete the full cycle. If you see a Phoenix staring at you from afar, keep your trigger finger ready on a stun to cancel the Dive. This is especially important with instant disables like hexes or Eulses or Force Staffs or Harpoons.
Phoenix cannot cast Icarus Dive when rooted/leashed, but roots/leashes won't cancel a Icarus Dive in progress.
Stunning, silencing, sleeping, cycloning, fearing, or hexing Phoenix during Sun Ray will cancel the spell.
Nyx Assassin makes life hard for the fire bird because it's not easy for Phoenix to stop dealing damage with Icarus Dive, Sun Ray, or even the Dying Light innate.

There are a lot of variables deciding this, but a good rule of thumb to follow is that you'll need 2 heroes to kill a level 1 Supernova Egg and 3 heroes to kill a level 2 Supernova Egg assuming you're all Fire Spirited right before Supernova is cast.

Heroes that buff attack speed (like Bloodseeker with Bloodrage, Marci with Unleash, Ogre Magi with Bloodlust, Snapfire with Lil' Shredder, Ursa with Overpower) or items that buff attack speed (Drum, Assault Cuirass) will help a lot with killing Supernovas.
You can kill the Supernova Egg during Naga Siren's Song of the Siren sleep.
Juggernaut can damage the Supernova Egg while right-clicking during Blade Fury.
Clones like Meepo and Arc Warden's Tempest Double count as heroes when attacking the Egg. Illusions do not and will deal no damage to a Supernova.

tips.text: Part of being a good Pudge is more than landing Hooks, but also knowing when your Hooks won't land. The cast time is long enough that you should be able to at least occasionally stop-cancel unlikely Hooks. Stop-canceling Hooks is also a great way to stress out enemies who can see you.

Arguably the most reliable way of predicting enemy movement for Hooks during the laning phase is to watch for last hits. While you're hiding, watch the HP of your creeps and wait for the enemy to pick up the last hit. The knowledge of where they will be plus their attack animation should be enough to land a Hook fairly easily. If the only thing between you and the enemy is a creep, start casting the Hook right before they complete the last hit so the Hook passes through the creep as it's dying.
You can pull runes using Meat Hook and the mana cost on Hook will be refunded. You can abuse this with Soul Ring to refund the 'temporary' mana provided by the Ring's active.
notes: This tech also works on any hero when interacting with Twin Gates, but it's a little trickier. Activate Soul Ring, start channeling a Twin Gate, and immediately cancel the channel. Every time you cancel a Twin Gate channel, you'll get the travel mana cost refunded. So if you spam cancel a bunch of Twin Gate channels, like 6 or so, you can fully replace the entire Soul Ring mana buffer with 'refunded' mana.

tips.text: Meat Hook will always bring the unit it caught to your cast location when the Hook finishes returning. With expert timing, you can use this mechanic to save allies who are being repositioned with spells (like Disruptor's Glimpse or Kunkka's X Marks the Spot) or catch escaping enemies (like an Io Relocate) by having them be mid-return-Hook when the repositioning spell is triggered.
notes: This also works with TPing allies to bring them back after they spend a split second in the fountain.
Meat Hook can pull allies or enemies out of Disruptor's Kinetic Field, Enigma's Black Hole, Faceless Void's Chronosphere, and Mars's Arena.
A rare exception to Meat Hook beating all other spells is Clockwerk's Power Cogs. If you're pulling an ally out of Power Cogs, Hook movement will get canceled by the shock from Cogs.

Meat Hook cannot pull allies or enemies that are being pulled by a Batrider's Flaming Lasso. However, if the Lasso ends mid-Hook, the target will end up next to Pudge once the Hook finishes returning.

tips.text: There are certain spots in the mid lane that you can jam your hero into that'll allow you to body block a Hook victim and prevent them from walking anywhere. Toss the Hook, then walk a tiny bit backwards to create a gap that only the victim can fit into.

Meat Hook does not cancel channels on allies. You can Hook them while they're TPing and it won't interrupt it. Hell, you can even Hook and move an allied Witch Doctor channeling Death Ward and it won't interrupt him.
Meat Hook damages, drags, and fully disables debuff immune/BKB'd enemies.
Meat Hook instantly kills any enemy/neutral non-ancient creep in connects with. This includes enemy siege creeps.
notes: Meat Hook can kill creeps through the Glyph or Roshan's Banner invulnerability.

tips.text: Meat Hook instantly kills enemy illusions.
Use Rot to help get last hits in lane.
You can't kill yourself with Rot damage.
You can toggle Rot while channeling, like during Dismember or a TP.
Meat Shield can be activated while channeling, like during Dismember or a TP.
Meat Shield reduces the self-damage taken from Rot.
Walking up to a hero and Dismembering them without Hooking them is like getting body shots as a Sniper in TF2. No one will respect you, but who cares when you get the kill.

Target and cast Dismember while an enemy is getting Hooked to give them as little time as possible to react with a BKB or some gap creating spell. This works because the sooner you start your Dismember cast animation, the less time an enemy has to react. If you start walking towards the enemy while they're returning from Hook, they'll be in Dismember cast range sooner.

When Roshing, don't use Dismember unless you're absolutely safe. It's a huge red flag for the enemy team that Pudge is off enjoying some fresh meat (the Dismember sound is global every time you cast it) despite the fact there is no hero on the map getting Benihana'd.

Don't ever shift-queue Meat Hook after Dismember. You are almost always better off canceling the last few milliseconds of Dismember by casting Meat Hook rather than waiting for the channel and cast backswing to end.
Dismember provides true sight on the target.
Never let Rubick steal Meat Hook. Constantly be spamming Rot against a Rubick.

counters.text: Play the hero and read the tips. The best way to beat a Pudge is to become the Pudge. You put Pudge into a cup, he becomes the cup, you put Pudge into a teapot, he becomes the teapot. Be Pudge, my friend.
Check Pudge's boots. If he's running at you with Rot and has Tranquils, you should right click him once to break his boots to slow his move speed before fleeing.
Lotus Orb prevents Pudge from casting Dismember on a target without it getting canceled instantly.
Dismember is a channeled disable, so stunning or silencing Pudge during the channel will end the spell.
In lane, consider constantly cutting down trees if you have a Quelling Blade. Pudge's Hooks are much easier to predict if he's not able to hide behind a forest.

tips.text: Plasma Field gives you flying vision as it travels out.
Static Link gives shared vision around the targeted hero.
Static Link fully works against debuff immune/BKB'd enemies.
Static Linking illusions steals damage just like on a hero.
You can Static Link creep-heroes like Brewmaster's Primal Split Brewlings, Visage Familiars, or Warlock's Golem.
The only thing that can stop Static Link is the enemy moving out of the break radius... or dying. Banishes or cyclones won't stop a Link in progress.
Mechanically, think of Static Link attacks as being similar to a short Windranger Focus Fire.
Static Link attacks scale with your attack speed.
Razor doesn't attack during Static Link if he's disarmed.

When moving in Static Link, you will face the direction you're clicking in, but once you stop clicking, Razor will turn around to face the enemy he's attacking. This is relevant when Static Linking a Medusa Stone Gazing so you can attack her and not get Stoned.

If for some reason you want to stop attacking a Static Linked target, like if they have Blade Mail active or they're under a Bane Nightmare, you can hold down the "Directional Move" command and mash your right click movement. You have to mash your move commands because each new directional move input cancels the Static Link attack animation.
notes: You can also hit the 'Cancel Current Action'/stop key and not move at all and Razor will just sit still without attacking anything. The moment you start moving, though, Razor will start attacking again.

tips.text: If you're worried more about dealing damage than stealing damage it's okay to Link the Crystal Maiden to buff up your damage if Luna keeps breaking the Link. You can sap more damage than a hero actually has, so CM will see a fat red -168 by her measly 63 damage.
Refreshing Static Link allows another Link to add another buff to Razor, but you can't double Link one target at the same time.
notes: If you Static Link multiple enemies at the same time, you can only get moving attacks on one of the targets, not both targets simultaneously.

tips.text: Refreshing Eye of the Storm fully stacks the spell.
Eye of the Storm prioritizes striking Static Linked heroes.
Eye of the Storm does not work on Roshan.
notes: Eye of the Storm does, however, work on the Tormentor.

tips.text: Eye of the Storm does not hit units in fog.

counters.text: Just because Razor died doesn't mean you get all your damage back instantly, and just because you died doesn't mean Razor won't keep dealing +200 damage. Static Link's buff/debuff will remain for the full duration.
Force Staff can help allies break the Static Link.
Razor won't right click during Static Link if he's disarmed.

Lotus Orb can discourage Razor from Static Linking allies. If a melee hero reflects a Static Link, the spell's internal attacks will only work if Razor is within 350 + melee hero attack range (default 150). Any further and the Static Link attacks will miss.
Eye of the Storm does not hit units in fog. No point trying to juke if you're Static Linked, however, because Static Link provides vision on the target.

tips.text: Tame the Beasts's fear will always cause enemies to run away in the direction opposite from Ringmaster's position. You can't fear an enemy to run into your hero no matter where they get hit by the whip's AoE, they'll always run away from you.
The "Debuff Immunity While Channeling Tame the Beasts" turns you debuff immune, but does not provide any kind of dispel on your hero.
Tame the Beasts and Impalement Arts can damage fogged and invis units.

Mechanically, think of Escape Act like placing Dark Willow's Shadow Realm on an ally. They can still be damaged and debuffed by ground targeted abilities, but unit targeted abilities and instant attacks can't hit them.
notes: That means allies also won't be able to target the hero in the Escape Act.

tips.text: The Escape Act buff disjoints any incoming projectiles on the target.
Escape Act can be targeted on illusions, clones, and creep-heroes.
If things are getting chaotic in a fight, know that you can target spells on allies, like Escape Act, by clicking on the allied hero's portrait in the top bar.
The Impalement Arts projectile gives vision as it travels and gives very brief vision when it impacts a target.

Multiple Impalement Arts do not stack on the same target. You'll get the impact damage for each new knife, but it'll only refresh the existing damage over time debuff if you re-Impale a target that's currently being stabbed.

The cast range on Impalement Arts is slightly longer than the maximum aggro range for neutral creeps. If you're trying to stack a camp with a dagger, you'll need to be within 1800 range of the camp for it to aggro you. Otherwise, they'll just sit in their spawn box contentedly being stabbed.
Agh's Shard Spotlight deals bonus damage against illusions.
Agh's Shard Spotlight provides vision in the circle AoEs and can briefly reveal invisible enemies that are caught.
Bumping an enemy with the Wheel of Wonder rollout does not count as a disable. You'll have to get them caught in the taunt to stun them.
Wheel of Wonder destroys trees as it travels and at its ending location.

Enemies need to be able to see the Wheel to get taunted by it. As tempting as it may look to drag the entire enemy team up on a cliff, it's risky casting Wheels there. Even if they look like they're facing it, it needs to be out of their fog of war to activate it.

Tame the Beasts's fear gives you some control over what direction enemies are facing. Toss the Wheel of Wonder behind an enemy and then hit them with Tame the Beasts so they turn around and stare into the Wheel to maximize disable time.
The Wheel of Wonder provides ground vision wherever it lands with the same day/night radius numbers as the average hero as well as flying vision over its damage AoE.
Mechanically, Souvenirs behave as items, not spells. This means that you can cast Souvenirs while silenced (but not when muted) and Rubick can't steal Souvenirs.
You will not get a Souvenir if you deny yourself to Roshan or neutral creeps.
Notes on the various Souvenirs:
notes: Funhouse Mirror is similar to a Manta Style activation in that it disjoints incoming projectiles and you can 'absorb' spells during the cast animation invulnerability period. However, you do not receive a dispel as you would with a Manta Style.
You can't cast Whoopee Cushion while rooted/leashed.
Strongman Tonic can be dispelled.

Riding the Unicycle is like a very fragile Pangolier Rolling Thunder. Any map cliffs Pango would "bounce" into will instead dismount your Unicycle. Additionally, bumping into enemy units or enemy structures also dismount you and running into trees will slow you down.
For the first 1.5s of Unicycle travel time, you can only be dismounted by bouncing into things. After that time, receiving any damage or disables from enemy heroes will also dismount you.
You can cast spells and activate most items while riding the Unicycle, but applying movement items to yourself, like Blink Dagger or Force Staff, will dismount you.
Starting any channels, like casting Tame the Beasts, using a TP scroll, or channeling a Watcher, will also dismount you.
You can dismount the Unicycle at any time by pressing the 'Cancel Current Action'/stop hotkey.
You can pick up runes on the Unicycle, but an illusion rune activation will dismount you because it's also a banish.

counters.text: Enemies can still be damaged and debuffed while in the Escape Act box by ground targeted abilities. Visually, they look invulnerable like in Tusk Snowball, but in actuality, it's more like they're in Dark Willow Shadow Realm.
You can knock the Escape Act box with forced movement spells like Clockwerk's Power Cogs or Keeper of the Light's Blinding Light to bump them out of the protection circle AoE.

Escape Act can be dispelled. This is relevant if you have a Nullifier or Shadow Demon's Demonic Purge to pre-cast onto a target who might get put into the box, or have access to ground targeted dispels like Brewmaster's Primal Split Dispel Magic or Oracle's Fortune's End to take them out of the box.

The Impalement Art daggers that emit from an Escape Act once Ringmaster has Agh's Scepter always shoot out the same way. If you're trying to dodge them, they're going to travel all eight cardinal and intercardinal directions at the same angles every time.
The Impalement Arts dagger projectile provides vision as it flies and briefly once it hits you, but the vision disappears when it starts stabbing you.
Be aware that Ringmaster can cast any of his Souvenirs while silenced.
The Strongman Tonic souvenir can be dispelled off targets.
You can only dismount Ringmaster off his Unicycle with damage after the first 1.5s of him wheeling around. Or you can just bump into him.

tips.text: Rubick's Curiosity innate debuff amplification is basically the opposite of status resistance in terms of mechanics.
It could be worth carrying Blood Grenades later in the game for an easy source of damage on enemy heroes to gain Curiosity innate stacks.

Telekinesis is a damn good disable mainly because Rubick has essentially non-existent cast times. For the most part, Telekinesis can be pulled off just as quickly as a hex. So if you're worried an initiator is about to Blink in and start a team fight, keep spam casting and canceling it on their initiator so that once they Blink in range, you'll instantly pick them up.

Telekinesis being instant allows you to steal spells that good players will usually avoid letting you get. If an Earthshaker just threw out a casual Fissure, they'll almost always cover it with Enchant Totem. However, if you pluck them out of the air with an instant Telekinesis disable, you can steal their spell before they get the chance to cast another.
You can continue changing the Telekinesis Land location until the spell goes off.
notes: However, Agh's Shard Telekinesis when targeted on allies will make them land as soon as you target Telekinesis Land rather than waiting the full duration.

tips.text: If a Telekinesed enemy gets affected by any items/spells that apply forced movement or knockback, they'll immediately drop straight down and stun the area underneath.
notes: When a Telekinesed unit dies, it also immediately drops down and stuns the AoE. You can pick up a weak creep and Fade Bolt it to death to instantly get an AoE Telekinsis stun.

tips.text: If you're getting chased by multiple heroes, it can be smart to cast the Land towards you, rather than away from you. During the Lift's duration, the other enemies will have probably passed your target up, so the Land should stun them on the way back.
Agh's Shard Telekinesis allows you to throw allies out of things like an enemy Disruptor's Kinetic Field or Slark's Pounce leash.
notes: You cannot Telekinesis allies out of Enigma's Black Hole, Faceless Void's Chronosphere, or Legion Commander's Duel, so don't even bother. It'll put the spell on cooldown and do nothing if you try.

tips.text: If things are getting chaotic in a fight, know that you can target spells on allies, like Agh's Shard Telekinsis, by clicking on the allied hero's portrait in the top bar.

One of the hallmarks of a strong anti-pusher is the ability to draw aggro from a creep wave off of a tower during pushes. Fade Bolt is probably one of the strongest spells in the game to do this, mainly because of its zero cast time, huge range, damage reduction ability, and substantial nuke damage. When you want to slow down the enemy's push, cast it on the creep wave and the creeps will lose interest in hammering your tower and come for you instead.
Fade Bolt bounces always take the shortest possible distance when jumping from target to target.
Fade Bolt will not bounce to enemies that aren't in vision. If you're Fade Bolting a creep wave at night time you'll only zap the creeps you see.
Fade Bolt loses damage with each bounce, so you should generally target the ranged creep first when trying to clear waves so you can actually get the last hit with full damage.
Arcane Supremacy cast range bonuses also apply to Rubick's items.
notes: This is also true for Curiosity innate bonuses.

tips.text: You can Spell Steal through debuff immunity. Just because Enigma is a big golden teardrop doesn't mean you can't steal Black Hole through BKB.
Patience is a virtue. Don't steal spells all willy nilly. Go into a team fight knowing the spells that you would want to steal and wait for them to be cast.
Different spells are useful at different stages of the game. Sure, most ultimates are almost always worth keeping, but other spells that help Rubick farm or scout can prove valuable during downtime.

Rubick has minimal cast times on any stolen spells. Forget everything you know about landing Leshrac's Split Earth, be amazed at how you can bust out an Earthshaker Fissure in a split second, and revel in how much better a spell Zeus's Lightning Bolt is when you don't have to fist pump for half a second to cast it.

Buffs/spells/summons lingering after a Spell Steal times out or if you Steal another Spell all follow different rules. You'll just have to play a bunch of Rubick to find out what works and what doesn't.
notes: Morph's Attribute Shift is a rare example of a spell that lasts not only after Spell Steal times out, but after death. Even after many deaths.

tips.text: Stolen spell cooldowns are persistent on Rubick. If a Spell Steal is about to time out and you're sad you never got to use your stolen Tidehunter Ravage, don't just cast it for giggles. You may end up screwing yourself over in a future team fight if you steal it again.

There is a slight delay as a stolen spell "projectile" travels to your hero. You can use this window to get one last cast of your previously stolen spell, like an invisibility spell, before the new one arrives.

You can globally check if an enemy hero is an illusion or not by attempting to cast Spell Steal on them. If you clicked on an illusion, you'll immediately get an error even if you're not in cast range.
Any stolen spells that have Agh's Scepter upgrades will automatically be upgraded if you have an Agh's Scepter.
Any stolen spells that have Agh's Shard upgrades will automatically be upgraded if you have an Agh's Shard.
While Agh's Scepter allows you steal two spells, if you steal a spell that takes two slots (like Puck's Illusory Orb + Ethereal Jaunt), you'll still lose your previously stolen spell.
You can't Spell Steal Morphling's Morph or Tinker's Rearm. Balance reasons? Or because it would simply cause too many programming headaches?
notes: However, you can Spell Steal from a Morphling who is in a Morph. You could theoretically duplicate one of your teammates spells this way.

tips.text: You can Spell Steal Faceless Void's Chronosphere but Void has a unique mechanic that allows him to move in any Chronosphere regardless of who cast it.

Spells that repeatedly drain mana, like Leshrac's Pulse Nova or Storm Sprit's Ball Lightning, do not have their draining mana cost reduced. Only the initial cost is reduced by Spell Steal. Mana cost reduction mechanics do not work on any abilities that drain mana over time on any hero.
You can use Earth Spirit's own Stone Remnants with your stolen versions of his spells.
With Agh's Shard, you can cast a stolen Life Drain into an enemy Pugna's Nether Ward.

counters.text: Rubick being in your lane automatically adds an extra danger range that you need to keep in your safety zone because of Telekinesis's repositioning ability. Don't let him into your zone.
Remember that Rubick has much better cast range on your abilities than you do thanks to Arcane Supremacy.

Rubick is all about capitalizing on your forgetfulness/laziness. "Oh right, they have a Rubick, I'm Tidehunter and I should have cast Anchor Smash after Ravage. I'm Mars and I should have cast Bulwark after Arena. I'm Batrider and I should have cast Sticky Napalm after Flaming Lasso." Put a condom on all of your spells, it's 99% effective.
Always check what spell Rubick has stolen by clicking on him. If you're Pudge and Rubick just Ghostbuster'd your essence, face your shame and tell your team that he has stolen Meat Hook, not Rot.

tips.text: The only reason you shouldn't hero target Burrowstrike is if you're going for multi-hero stuns or if you're trying to achieve a very specific position. Unlike Lion's Earth Spike, the bonus range granted by skillshotting Burrowstrike is barely anything (~100 units extra).
Burrowstrike ignores Linken's Sphere and Lotus Orbs.
Burrowstrike is a movement spell that doesn't destroy trees in its path. This can be useful when trying to juke and escape pursuers.

Sand King isn't actually 'traveling' during Burrowstrike. It's more like you turn into a projectile and teleport to your destination. As a result, you'll completely bypass any spells that may be in Burrowstrike's path (like Dark Willow's Bramble Maze, Jakiro's Ice Path, or even a Faceless Void's Chronosphere).
notes: You can use this mechanic to even dodge spells like Disruptor's Glimpse or Kunkka's X Marks. If you time the Burrowstrike perfectly so that the enemy's repositioning spell goes off during your travel time, Burrowstrike movement will override Glimpse/X's movement.

tips.text: Attacking or casting an item/spell while in the Sand Storm AoE will temporarily reveal you for a brief period of time, but you'll go back invis after.
notes: If your Burrowstrike ends within Sand Storm's AoE, there will be no fade time on you re-entering invisibility.
You can remove Dust detection (after you walk out of the AoE) with basic dispels, like from Eul's, Guardian Greaves, or Lotus Orb.

tips.text: When farming jungle camps with Sand Storm, it's sometimes advantageous to be visible so that the neutrals won't run around aimlessly. You can cast an empty Bottle or spam Power Tread swapping to stay out of invis.

Stinger's damage is applied as an instant attack . This instant attack ignores disarms, has true strike, and applies attack modifiers (except cleave). If you have an attack modifier with a proc, it'll roll for a chance to proc on each target hit.
notes: Since Stinger is an instant attack, it'll break your Smoke if it damages a unit.

tips.text: You can use your 'Cancel Current Action'/stop hotkey to cancel your Epicenter cast animation without putting it on cooldown.

If you're planning on casting Epicenter post-Burrowstrike, aim the Burrowstrike so you end up behind the enemy. This'll buy you a turn animation's amount of time before they can spin around and attempt to interrupt your Epicenter cast.

If you're going to shift-queue your Blink Dagger after the Epicenter animation, choose your destination at the very last second. Things can change during the long ass cast animation. Positions can move, TPs come in, Blinks go out, empires fall.
If enemies have vision of any part of the Agh's Shard Epicenter AoE, the whole spell is shown through fog.
Agh's Shard Epicenter pulses trigger on invisible and fogged units.

counters.text: Dust can be very irritating for Sand King to deal with since he'll have to leave the reveal AoE for the invisibility on Sand Storm to be useful.
Essence Distiller can provide true sight on the debuffed target, such as Sand King in Sand Storm.
Sand King cannot Burrowstrike when rooted/leashed.
Sand King's Caustic Finale innate won't trigger if a unit is denied.

tips.text: Your Fowl Play innate will not protect you from a lethal Axe Culling Blade or Necrophos Reaper's Scythe.
notes: It will protect you from a lethal amount of damage after Oracle's False Promise ends, though.

tips.text: Ether Shock can hit secondary units almost twice as far away than the spell's cast range. If an enemy is making a run for it and is just out of cast range, try casting the Shock on the ranged creep right behind them to possibly hit them. Ether Shock won't bounce to units that are in fog, however.
Ether Shock chooses secondary targets in a cone in front of Shadow Shaman. Secondary targets are always the closest available units to the primary target.

The facts on Hex: Instant cast time, insta-kills illusions (except 'strong' illusions like Venge's Agh's Scepter Vengeance illusion), and is super annoying. Spam cast and cancel this spell on the enemy team's initiator when you're toeing off. The moment they Blink in and are in range, they'll be Rhasta Fried Chicken.
notes: Hexes are effectively casting a silence, a mute, and a slow on enemies. Some enemies can cast spells while stunned (like Abaddon with Borrowed Time), but can't during a hex because they're silenced.

tips.text: An enemy will always be able to activate BKB in-between Shackle and Hex. Lead with Hex during ganks, especially since Hex has no cast animation and also has longer range.
Shackles provides true sight on the target.
You can cast Agh's Scepter Shackles on any couriers on your team and use them as Ether Shocking drones. Just be aware of the break distance.
You can trap enemies inside your Wards by targeting the circle directly onto a hero. Unless they have something like Phase Boots, they'll be trapped by the collision of all the Wards.
Serpent Wards are controllable units. Be sure to keep Wards focused on your most important target, like the enemy tower, before they got distracted in a team fight.
Serpent Wards can attack other types of ward units, like Pugna's Nether Ward or Undying's Tombstone.

Don't let enemies farm your Serpent Wards for free after they win a team fight. It only takes a few attacks from a hero to kill a Ward. Select one lone Ward in the back and have it murder its siblings with a deny when they're down to 1 HP.
Serpent Wards have 1200/800 day/night vision.
Serpent Wards can benefit from the attack speed buff provided by Chen's Penitence.
Serpent Wards are frozen inside Faceless Void's Chronosphere. Place the Wards outside of the Chrono if you want to hit enemies inside.
Tier 1 towers never have backdoor protection enabled, only Tier 2 onwards have it. Keep this in mind if you want to sneak a quick Tier 1 tower with Serpent Wards without a creep wave.

Sentry wards can tank ten hits from a tower before they die. If you're trying to sneakily take a tower and you really want to make sure it goes down, consider plopping down a sentry ward to draw the tower's aggro and then casting Serpent Wards. I guess you could also burn an observer ward for this strat, but you better have a huge lead if you're doing that.

counters.text: If you're trapped in a circle of Serpent Wards, you can Phase through the Serpents using Phase Boots or certain invis abilities.
Damage block does not mitigate Serpent Ward damage. All ward-type units ignore damage block, like from Vanguard.
Casting Serpent Wards costs a ton of mana, making Shaman a great candidate for mana burning or Pugna Nether Warding against.
Illusion attacks count as hero attacks against Serpent Wards.
You can break these cuffs. Always have a stun/silence ready on your team to bail a teammate out from the Shackle channel.
notes: Banishes can also free allies from channeled disables, like Shackles.

counters.text: Lotus Orb can help discourage Shadow Shaman from chain disabling allies.

Keep a Blood Grenade handy in lane to finish off a Shadow Shaman who may otherwise narrowly escape with his Fowl Play innate. Just be sure to cast it after the innate procs because it also dispels him on trigger.
Breaks can disable Shadow Shaman's Fowl Play innate.
notes: Breaks can be provided with items like Silver Edge or Khanda. Spells that Break include Doom's Agh's Scepter Doom, Hoodwink's Sharpshooter, Naga Siren's Agh's Scepter Ensnare, Nyx Assassin's Vendetta, Phantom Assassin's Agh's Scepter Fan of Knives, Shadow Demon's Agh's Scepter Demonic Purge, Viper's Viper Strike, and a few others.

counters.text: A lethal Axe Culling Blade or Necrophos Reaper's Scythe can kill Shadow Shaman through his Fowl Play innate.

tips.text: You can cast Guardian Sprint while TPing and it won't cancel the channel.
Guardian Sprint gives Slardar 100% slow resistance for the first few seconds of the buff.
Slithereen Crush's puddle and the water trail from Corrosive Haze buffs your Seaborn Sentinel innate the same way being in the river would.
notes: Make a puddle with Crush when pushing towers to benefit from the bonus passive damage from Seaborn Sentinel.

tips.text: Slithereen Crush and Bash procs deal physical damage, making them work very well with Corrosive Haze's armor reduction.
Increase your Bash attack counter on jungle or lane creeps. The buff lasts indefinitely and won't increase/proc on building or ward targets.
Basher/Abyssal passive bashes don't work with Slardar. The game won't allow you to have another bash besides Bash of the Deep.
Bash of the Deep can stun enemies through spell immunity/BKB.
Corrosive Haze's armor reduction makes taking Rosh or Tormentor much easier for your team.
Corrosive Haze's true sight isn't some sort of get-out-of-buying-detection-free card. The way to counter invis heroes is to know where they are before they know you know where they are.
Corrosive Haze fully works on debuff immune/BKB'd enemies.
You can cast Corrosive Haze on enemy couriers.

counters.text: Slardar's Guardian Sprint can be dispelled.
Guardian Sprint gives Slardar 100% slow resistance for the first few seconds of the buff.
Be aware that Corrosive Haze's armor reduction can allow the enemy team to take Roshan super early.
Corrosive Haze provides true sight on any debuffed targets.
Corrosive Haze can be removed with basic dispels like from Lotus Orb, Guardian Greaves, Manta Style, Disperser, or Satanic.
notes: Slardar has a "Corrosive Haze Undispellable" talent.

tips.text: Capitalize on Essence Shift innate stacks. Take a tower or TP to another lane and use all the damage you have to continue snowballing. Don't just sit around and farm, the enemy should be scared of how much damage you have after winning a fight.
You will lose all Essence Shift innate stacks on death, including deaths from Aegis. The enemies will still be missing their stats for the full duration, however.
You need to be within 300 range of a target dying with the Essence Shift innate debuff to get the permanent AGI. Or if you get the kill credit, the enemy can be at any range.
Each tick of Dark Pact strong dispels Slark. In addition to most standard debuffs, strong dispels can even remove stuns.

Dark Pact can't remove a lot of things despite being a strong dispel. A few undispellable debuffs worth keeping in mind are: Ancient Apparition's Ice Blast, Bloodseeker's Rupture, Invoker's Deafening Blast, Witch Doctor's Maledict, Razor's Static Link, Ursa's Fury Swipes, or Viper's Viper Strike. If you want to get rid of these spells, too bad.

Dark Pact is a 'nuke' like Lifestealer's Infest can be a 'nuke.' Yes, the spell can deal healthy damage, but that's not its only purpose. Don't yank the Pact ripcord the second you get in melee range of your gank target. Wait for them to turn around, or for their teammate to come in to save them, then pull the trigger and wipe off any potential disable. If you need to use Dark Pact for damage, only use it if you're sure the enemy can't disable you or try to save it for the killing blow.
Pounce won't latch illusions, making it useful for identifying the real Chaos Knight/Phantom Lancer/Naga Siren.
Pounce can hit and leash invisible units, but it won't give any vision of them.
Pounce connects with debuff immune/BKB'd targets and you will get Essence Shift innate stacks, but the leash won't restrict their movement.
Leashing enemies with Pounce can cancel TPs and prevent them from casting most movement spells while leashed. Mechanically, leashes function very similarly to roots.
Take advantage of your free pathing state in Pounce when you're escaping. Don't just leap along down the lane, jump over a tree line or clear a cliff to create a gap.

Orienting Pounces to go where you want them to can sometimes be challenging when the game's pathing doesn't cooperate. A handy way to work around this is by enabling the "Holding ALT Enables Directional Move" option in settings. This command makes it so that whenever you're holding down ALT, your hero ignores pathing and tries to move in a straight line towards where you right clicked.
notes: You can also enable the "Directional Move" hotkey in the settings, but this ALT modifier may be easier to use once you get used to it.
Directional move can also be helpful for aiming spells when escaping over cliffs like Mirana's Leap, Pangolier's Shield Crash, Ursa's Earthshock, or Zeus's Heavenly Jump.

tips.text: The passive from Shadow Dance can be very useful for counterwarding. If you're walking around and you lose the Shadow Dance regen buff, you'll know you've wandered into enemy vision.
notes: So carry your own sentry wards. I'm serious. Yes, I know you're a carry, you've probably never clicked on the item in your life, but do it. Did you know observer wards give gold when you kill them? It's a net profit, I promise.

tips.text: Enemies can still see the TP particle effect when you start channeling under Shadow Dance.
Slark is one of few heroes that has 1800 night vision.
You can't cast Shadow Dance while channeling a TP unlike other invis spells, but you can activate Shadow Blade/Silver Edge mid-channel.

counters.text: Slark's Essence Shift innate is the long con. You may think you're winning these exchanges in lane because Slark has awful HP, but he's gaining a Slipper of Agility and you're losing an Iron Branch's worth of stats every time you trade hits.
You'll get your Essence Shifted stats back when you respawn, but Slark will still have them as well. This is true for Aegis respawns as well.

Dark Pact strong dispels as often as it damages, meaning that there are 10 little mini-dispels throughout the duration of the spell. So don't bother trying to stun Slark mid-Pact, just wait for the spell to end.

If Slark Pounces on you, don't just immediately mash your stuns on him. Bad Slarks usually pop Dark Pact the moment they jump on someone because most enemies panic and use their disables as soon as this fishy boy starts stabbing them. Instead, accept the fact that you got caught, gamble that a Dark Pact is about to come out, then use your stun after you see Pact used.
notes: If you're playing against a smart Slark, you can go one layer deeper and cast and cancel your stun spell animation to bait out the Dark Pact.
Keep an eye on his mana bar to verify if he actually cast Dark Pact or not.

counters.text: Ground targeted spells (especially ground targeted stuns like Lina's Light Strike Array, Leshrac's Split Earth, Nyx's Impale, etc) are highly valuable against Slark for hassling him whenever he activates Shadow Dance.

Inexperienced Slarks have a tendency of going for long-range Pounces which are fairly easy to juke. Line yourself up with him when you're getting chased to tease the Pounce out, then move straight left or right and dodge it.

If you manage to move your hero outside the edge of the Pounce leash, it'll break. That means weird things that provide collision, like planting an Iron Branch or getting shoved by Earthshaker Fissure or Tusk Ice Shards will break the leash. So do other repositioning spells, like getting kicked by an Earth Spirit Boulder Smash, getting Meat Hooked by Pudge, or even a lucky Manta Style rearrangement.
notes: If you go for the Manta Style method, your best bet is to activate Phase Boots before Mirror Image to reduce your chances of collision with an illusion pushing you back into the leash.

If you go for the Branch planting method, either portrait casting or casting the Branch inside your hero's selection circle between your hero model and the leash is surprisingly reliable at breaking out of a Pounce. This Branch trick also works against Disruptor's Kinetic Field.

counters.text: You can't Force Staff out of Slark's Pounce leash, but you can break the leash by Hurricane Piking any target that isn't yourself.
notes: Piking any target that isn't yourself works. You can even Pike an ally, which is theoretically just like using a Force Staff on them, and it'll free you from Pounce leash.
However, if an ally is Pounce leashed, you can't use Pike on them to save them.

counters.text: Debuff immunity/BKB allows you to walk out of Slark's Pounce leash.
If Slark is trying to escape, attempt to intercept his Pounce out by standing in front of him so he'll hit your hero instead of making a getaway over a cliff.
Slark cannot Pounce when rooted/leashed.
Slark's Essence Shift innate gaining new stacks and HP regen from the Shadow Dance passive can both be disabled by breaks.
notes: Breaks can be provided with items like Silver Edge or Khanda. Spells that Break include Doom's Agh's Scepter Doom, Hoodwink's Sharpshooter, Naga Siren's Agh's Scepter Ensnare, Nyx Assassin's Vendetta, Phantom Assassin's Agh's Scepter Fan of Knives, Shadow Demon's Agh's Scepter Demonic Purge, Viper's Viper Strike, and a few others.
Silver Edge and Khanda's Breaks are especially strong against Slark since they cannot be dispelled.

counters.text: Ghost Scepter can help supports survive Slark ganks.
Ancient Apparition's Ice Blast can prevent Slark from healing even during his active Shadow Dance and can't be dispelled.

Bloodseeker notably counters the dickens out of Slark. Slark doesn't like to be silenced, he can't Dark Pact off Rupture, and if he loses too much HP he'll make BS Thirsty and give him global true sight, thus preventing his Shadow Dance passive regen.
Spirit Breaker is irritating for Slark to deal with since Dark Pact can't dispel Charge and since Charge will provide vision the whole time, Slark can't regen with his Shadow Dance passive.
Slark can't dispel Disruptor's Glimpse, making the full combo of Static Storm+Kinetic Field often lethal.
Naga Siren's Song turns off Slark's Shadow Dance active and reveals him, thus stopping Slark from regening and being invisible. The Dance will continue once the Song ends, though.
Gleipnir can root Slark even when he's untargetable in Shadow Dance.

Dust has a weird interaction with Dark Pact + Shadow Dance. Dust applies damage to any targets that are "invisible." While Shadow Dance isn't traditional invisibility that gets revealed by Dust, Dust still damages a Slark in Shadow Dance anyway. The funny part is if Slark activates Dark Pact while under Shadow Dance in Dust's AoE, he'll get damaged for every single time Dust gets purged off and then instantly reapplied.
notes: Dust damaging weird types of invisibility also applies to Dusting enemies who are Smoked. Could be a clever way to break Blink Daggers if you're being ganked.

tips.text: Multiple casts of Shrapnel on the same area don't stack.
Use Shrapnel to provide vision of the enemy tower during high ground sieges if your creeps are dead.
Tier 1 towers never have backdoor protection enabled, only Tier 2 onwards have it. Keep this in mind if you want to sneak a quick Tier 1 tower without a creep wave.
You can use the active on Take Aim to prevent Rubick from stealing your better spells.
You can cancel the long Assassination cast animation with the 'Cancel Current Action'/stop key.
Assassinate ministuns targets and can break enemy channels when the projectile lands.
Assassinate gives true sight on the target during the cast animation and until the projectile connects.

Assassinate provides shared vision around the target. This is useful when dealing with high ground (sieging or defending) since you can keep casting it and canceling it on enemies/creeps to see around them.
If Sniper gets a kill, Assassinate's cooldown is refreshed. You don't even need to get the kill with Assassinate, any kill refreshes it.

Assassinate applies an instant attack in addition to the nuke damage. This instant attack ignores disarms, has true strike, and applies attack modifiers. If you have an attack modifier with a proc, it'll roll for a chance once the projectile lands.
notes: You can activate Take Aim before the projectile lands to get the guaranteed Headshot proc on the instant attack.
You can activate Shadow Blade/Silver Edge after the Assassinate projectile is launched to get the backstab damage.
Since Assassinate deals an instant attack, it'll break your Smoke once it damages a unit.

tips.text: The hero that needs to exploit positioning in lane the most. The Sniper Shuffle is the complex laning dance that involves waddling forward, peeping the enemy in the face until you get a Headshot, pissing them off, running backwards, praying that they don't feel like wasting the energy to kill you, waiting for them to retreat, then repeating. The better you are at predicting enemy movement, the better Sniper you can be.
Agh's Shard Concussive Grenade counts as a disable, allowing you to briefly stun enemies and cancel their channels.
The self-knockback from Agh's Shard Concussive Grenade allows you to travel up and down cliffs. You can even blast yourself out of a Disruptor's Kinetic Field.

Nullifier can dispel the Force Staff buff off heroes. However, Hurricane Pike still kind of works. If you're trying to escape while Nullified, you'll be able to create more distance by Piking a pursuing enemy away rather than using Pike as a self-Force Staff.
Sniper has higher than average night vision (1400 vs the standard 800). If you only barely see someone at night, chances are they can't see you.

counters.text: If you're getting Assassinated, you will have a debuff icon present in your status bar. The shot will get fired when the debuff timer goes around halfway. There are a few ways to evade it:
notes: Since the spell gives true sight on your hero, it can't be disjointed by traditional invisibility. However, Smoke of Deceit invis is unique and will cancel the targeting or even disjoint the projectile.
Other disjoints, like from Blinks, will only dodge the spell after the projectile is fired.

Spells that banish you or make you untargetable will cancel the Assassination cast. You don't need to time it when the projectile is fired, banishes cancel the targeting phase of Assassination. This even includes the very quick banish from a Manta Style activation.

Going invulnerable, like from Bane's Nightmare or being cycloned in Eul's, will cancel Assassinate's targeting cast. Or you can go for sick nasty plays and make him waste his cooldown and go invulnerable after the Assassinate projectile is fired.

counters.text: Infused Raindrop can save your life from some early game Assassinations.
Sniper has higher than average night vision (1400 vs the standard 800). Something to be aware of if you're trying to gank him at night.
Sniper will not receive the knockback from Agh's Shard Concussive Grenade if he's rooted or leashed.

tips.text: When farming neutral camps, kill the smaller creeps first. That way you can proc your Desolate innate damage on the big creep.
Spectral Dagger gives shared vision on every enemy that get hits by the projectile. This allows you to get basic vision (not true sight, just location) on invis enemies.

If your hero is within ~1800 range of a neutral camp, you can draw aggro and stack it if you damage the camp, like with Spectral Dagger. Any further away and neutrals won't aggro your hero when damaged and just keep sitting in their camp.
Spectral Dagger ignores Lotus Orbs.
Spectral Dagger can bypass Linken's Sphere if ground targeted.

Spectre gets a 1 second grace period of free pathing after walking off a Spectral Dagger trail. So if you're trying to escape and don't need to create a huge gap, you can toss the Dagger at your enemies to slow them and then escape backwards over a cliff or across some trees.
Spectre illusions can also benefit from the Spectral Dagger trail's free pathing.
You can't use Spectral Dagger's free pathing to get out of spells like Disruptor's Kinetic Field or Mars's Arena, but you can Reality to an illusion that's outside to escape.

Shadow Step illusions have a long enough duration to allow you to toss one out, TP back to base, get some regen or grab items from your stash, then Reality back to the illusion (assuming they didn't kill it).
Dispersion reflects damage before any reductions are calculated. This means it will deal damage before calculating any armor/magic resistance/barriers.
Spectre doesn't have a farming steroid like most carries. However, Haunt allows her to perpetually farm lanes or split push since she can instantly participate in a team fight on demand.

You're invulnerable when flying to an illusion when casting Reality. You can use this to run head first into projectiles like Gyrocopter's Homing Missile to negate the stun/damage. If your timing is godlike, you can even use the travel invulnerability to dodge things like the AoE stun from Phoenix's Supernova.
You can use Reality multiple times during a Haunt cast.
If a target dies, the corresponding Haunt illusion will vanish as well.
Casting Haunt can be a handy way to break enemy initiator Blink Daggers even if you don't have vision of them.

counters.text: Spectral Dagger creates a trail on invis units if you took damage from the spell.
Shadow Step and Haunt illusions have free pathing and will follow you over cliffs. These illusions can be slowed and stunned.
Any level of Dagon can instakill illusions. As do spells like Disruptor's Glimpse, Pudge's Meat Hook, Skywrath Mage's Mystic Flare, and any Hex.
notes: Brewmaster's Storm Brewling with Dispel Magic deals full damage to all types of illusions.

counters.text: Enchantress can take control of enemy illusions with Enchant.

Whenever Spectre Shadow Steps, stand next to your creeps or give your teammates a hug. For most of the early to mid game her only illusion damage is coming from her Desolate innate, so don't let it proc.
Spectre's Desolate innate and Dispersion passives can be disabled by breaks.
notes: Breaks can be provided with items like Silver Edge or Khanda. Spells that Break include Doom's Agh's Scepter Doom, Hoodwink's Sharpshooter, Naga Siren's Agh's Scepter Ensnare, Nyx Assassin's Vendetta, Phantom Assassin's Agh's Scepter Fan of Knives, Shadow Demon's Agh's Scepter Demonic Purge, Viper's Viper Strike, and a few others.

counters.text: Mage Slayer reduces all spell damage from enemies, potentially making it useful at mitigating Dispersion or Desolate innate damage from Spectre.
Spectres generally don't like building BKB or MKB, so magic damage and evasion may prove to be more useful against her compared to other carries.
Spectre cannot travel to illusions with Reality if she's rooted.

tips.text: Take advantage of the proximity Greater Bashes you are gifted while Charging. If you're trying to land a stun on a unit that can't be targeted by Charge (if they're cycloned, banished, Linken's Sphere'd, etc) line yourself up so that you can cast Charge on a unit behind your intended target so you'll bash them en route.

Charge is blocked by Linken's Sphere on cast. You can potentially outplay this by Charging a creep near where your target is farming and hoping the creeps die so the Charge target will shift to the hero. A substitute Charge will not pop Linken's.

If you see an opportunity to gank another lane, consider TPing to the nearest available structure before casting a cross-country Charge. The less time an enemy has to react and reposition, the more successful your ganks will be.
If you're getting ganked and you can't take the fight, immediately move your camera over to another lane, find a creep or neutral, and Charge it. This is your escape mechanism.
You can send your courier to give vision of neutral camps to sneakily Charge around the map.
In your buffs, there is a portrait of the hero you're Charging. You can alt+click this to announce to your team who you're targeting with Charge.

During Charge, you are granted shared vision around the target. That means fog of war is removed around whatever the enemy hero can see. This is especially useful against heroes who have extra vision in certain situations, like a Night Stalker in Dark Ascension.

If you want to throw enemies off your Charge trajectory or slightly stall a Charge, consider backpacking move speed items while you're Charging. You'll slow yourself down and enemies may think you canceled the Charge.
Charge has literally no consistency whatsoever against Disruptor's Kinetic Field. Sometimes you'll get stuck on the edge, sometimes you'll pass through unimpeded. I have no clue what controls this.
You can cast non-targeted items while you're Charging, like Phase Boots, Shadow Blade, Mask of Madness, Smoke of Deceit, BKB, and even Power Tread switching.

You can cast Bulldoze while Charging. Charge applies a Greater Bash on everything you hit and Greater Bash deals damage based off your move speed, so activating Bulldoze mid-Charge will boost your damage on contact.
notes: You can also cast Agh's Shard Planar Pocket while Charging.

tips.text: After your Charge connects on an enemy, you'll usually have enough time to fish for one Greater Bash right click in the stun duration before you need to chain into Nether Strike.

Greater Bash's proc chance utilizes pseudo-random distribution (PRD). Statistically, about one in every six right clicks should be a Bash with 17%, but PRD encourages a lower likelihood of 'streaks.' If you go six right clicks with no Bash, chances are now much higher that your next right click will Bash thanks to PRD. Try to exploit this by priming right clicks on jungle or lane creeps before going for a gank.
Basher/Abyssal passive bashes don't work with Spirit Breaker. The game won't allow you to have another bash besides Greater Bash.
Greater Bash can stun enemies through spell immunity/BKB.

Greater Bash is essentially a crit dressed up in a scaling bash. Unfortunately, the only way of amplifying the 'crit' damage is by building move speed, not damage. The plus side is that you have two guaranteed ways of proccing this crit Bash with Charge and Nether Strike.
You can Nether Strike enemy couriers, but it won't damage them.
Probably the best Dust carrier and anti-invis hero you could ask for in pubs. Every time Dust is off cooldown, Charge that Cloak and Dagger'd Riki and bash him into next Tuesday.

Get wards in the enemy jungle. Players will automatically avoid farming in lane once they realize you're becoming a threat and will start farming their jungle. Teach them that there is no sanctuary from the space cow.
SB is one of the tankiest level 1 heroes in the game. Take advantage of your chuftiness and don't be afraid of getting into fights early on.

Mechanically, Agh's Shard Planar Pocket is like putting an inverse Linken's Sphere buff on a target. Enemy unit-targeted spells or items will do nothing to the Planer Pocketed target and will instead get re-cast from the enemy onto you. This includes any unit-targeted buffs that an enemy may place on their ally. If you're curious about the nuanced quirks and features of this spell, feel free to consult the wiki.

counters.text: Ward everywhere. You need to always be keeping tabs on Spirit Breaker: Where does he come from, where does he go, who is he ganking, Barathrum Joe.

Even though most Spirit Breakers will carry Dust, consider getting a Glimmer Cape if he's Charging often. Nearly all of SB's damage is magical and needs to be dealt quickly, so the magic damage barrier while Glimmered can soak up a lot of his gank potential.
Charge can break Linken's from across the map. In Herald scum pubs this makes Linken's a Spirit Breaker counter, but in RIAA-certified Double Immortal tier, this makes SB a Linken's counter.

Remember that SB gets increased status resistance while in Bulldoze. Status resistance affects many things. It also doesn't affect a lot of things you may think it does. Here's the wiki page with all the interactions.

One of the easiest heroes to bait. No SB can resist Charging down a lonely Crystal Maiden quietly farming in lane, so take advantage of the mad cow's blood thirst. After a few failed ganks, the map will open up substantially when he stops Charging on a whim.
notes: Remember that while you're Charged, Spirit Breaker reveals the same fog of war that your hero sees. So don't just stand next to allies in plain sight if you're baiting him, make sure they're hiding behind trees where your hero wouldn't be able to naturally see them.

counters.text: SB can't cast Charge or Nether Strike when rooted/leashed.
Bulldoze can be removed off Spirit Breaker with basic dispels. This makes Eul's a handy item against him.
Shadow Demon can be a pretty strong counterpick with banishes to protect allies and Demonic Purge to slow SB and remove Bulldoze.

You can stun/root SB while he's Charging to cancel it. This is useful to know when you're getting Charged, but it's also useful when you're ganking SB. Keep a stun in your pocket for when he tries to Charge to another lane to escape.
notes: Force Staff, Harpoon, and other sources of forced movement or knockback can also end Charge prematurely.

counters.text: Force Staff (or any other source of forced movement or knockback) will instantly remove Greater Bash's stun debuff. If an ally is stunned by Spirit Breaker's right click or Nether Strike, you can Force Staff them and they'll immediately be unstunned.
notes: This tip will not work against Charge, however. Charge has its own built in stun mechanic, only stuns using Greater Bash's debuff can be taken off with forced movement.

counters.text: You can disable SB while he's in the middle of the cast animation for Nether Strike to interrupt the animation.

tips.text: Storm Hammer stuns and damages everything in its AoE. If an enemy has Linken's Sphere, but is sitting inside their creep wave, just target the Hammer on a creep.
Warcry works fully on illusions and creep-heroes (Brewmaster's Primal Split Brewlings, Visage's Familiars, or Warlock's Golem).

God's Strength multiplies Sven's primary attribute/base damage. Meaning, when you go full WOLOLO, only damage from STR is getting multiplied, but items that are adding green + damage (raw damage items) aren't get multiplied.
Agh's Scepter Storm Hammer can dispel things like Ghost Scepter or spells like Windranger's Windrun off enemies.
notes: The dispel affects everything in the AoE, meaning you can even dispel Ringmaster's Escape Act or a Eul's cyclone if they're in the AoE.

tips.text: Unlike most mobility spells, Agh's Scepter Storm Hammer is not disabled by roots/leashes. You can even travel in and out of Mars's Arena thanks to the invulnerability as well.

counters.text: Storm Hammer's projectile can be disjointed.
Warcry can be removed off Sven and his allies with basic dispels.
notes: Agh's Shard Warcry cannot be dispelled.

counters.text: Cleave damage, like from Great Cleave, can be reduced by armor.
Breaks can disable Sven's Wrath of God innate and Great Cleave.
At a certain point in the game, Sven chunks so hard that you won't even be able to react and survive his initiation. An Aeon Disk could save your life in these situations.

tips.text: The bonus damage charges you get on Refraction don't get consumed on denial attacks, but you also don't get the bonus damage when issuing deny attacks.
Since the entire damage instance is blocked, Refraction prevents Blink Dagger or consumable regen from breaking if you get hit.

You can survive a potentially lethal Oracle's False Promise by activating Refraction right before the spell times out. This is because the entirety of damage received (or heal received) during False Promise is delivered in one instance which can be absorbed by a single Refraction barrier.
Before going in for a gank or joining a team fight, you want a fully charged Refraction to be on the tail end of its timer so you can put a fresh one up when everything inevitably starts going wrong.

Meld has no cast time and no fade time. This is useful for disjointing spells, tower shots, and right clicks, but it's also huge for juking. When you're getting chased, Meld as soon as you get a moment of high ground above the enemies. If you're juking in the jungle, Meld as soon as you think you're in a split-second of fog. Chances are the enemy will assume you kept running and continue chasing the same direction.
You have no collision when you're Melded, so you won't block pathways.
If you have trouble landing Meld strikes in the heat of the moment, try using attack+move commands instead of right clicking on the enemy.
The armor reduction debuff from Meld works on Rosh. The debuff stacks as well, so you should try to double-Meld Rosh when you first start taking it.
Meld damage and the armor reduction debuff will be applied to all units the attack Psi Blade spills onto.
The "Meld Hit Bash" talent can stun enemies through debuff immunity/BKB.
The "Meld Hit Bash" talent will stun everyone who gets hit by the Meld spill.

To be an effective Lanaya, you've got to learn how to play Psi Blades like a concert pianist. A deny could be used to pick up a last hit in the same stroke. A full creep wave should be wiped in two spills after you pick up a Desolator. Move creeps and neutrals in the jungle around to get the perfect spills.

Psi Blade's spill angle is calculated from TA's position once the attack connects, not from where TA was when the attack was started. It's not much, but you can ever so slightly move yourself around after you launch an attack projectile to change spill angles onto the enemy.

You can target your Traps with deny attacks to give a target to Psi Blade spill off of. If an enemy is escaping out of your attack range or vision, try planting a Trap in a line behind them and immediately deny it to potentially spill onto the enemy.
notes: You can even spill Meld damage off of denying attacks.

tips.text: Psi Blade spill damage can hit ethereal units. If enemies have Ghost Scepters, you can try damaging the target by deny attacking your Traps to spill damage onto the enemy.
Psi Blade spill damage can hit invisible units.

Psi Blade damage can spill through Venomancer's Plague Wards, Techies' Proximity Mines, and Tinker's Deploy Turrets, but not any other types of ward units (other than your Traps). Probably because other ward units require a flat number of attacks to kill, but the Spillable ones have actual HP.
notes: However, Meld damage can spill through all ward units. Like if you're attacking a Phoenix Supernova egg, Psi Blade spills won't deal damage to targets behind the egg, but a Meld spill can.

tips.text: You can give shared control of your Traps to all of your teammates so they can detonate your Traps themselves by opening the scoreboard and clicking the "Show Shared Unit Control Options" icon in the bottom corner. Please notify your teammates that you're doing this otherwise you're going to sabotage their micro.

The core early game Trap locations for vision are the runes (or at least one rune) and choke points on stairs. Mid/late game should include Traps on the Twin Gates and jungle camps the enemy may like to farm.
notes: Traps don't give vision when placed inside the Rosh pit, but it's still worth putting a Trap in front of the pit entrance so you can catch when the enemy may be walking in to Rosh.

tips.text: Towers are extremely slow at killing Traps. If you're diving, you can plant a Trap in tower aggro range without fear of it immediately dying to tower shots.
Damage from multiple Traps won't stack.
The last Trap debuff an enemy is hit by will immediately overwrite the previous Trap debuff (for both the slow and damage).
If you are within ~1800 range of a neutral camp, you can draw aggro and stack it with Psionic Trap damage. Be sure to account for the Trap slow affecting the neutrals with your stack timings.
If you're close to messing up a stack, try using a Trap to slow down the neutrals before they make it back inside their spawn box.
You can use Trap damage on lane creeps to split push lanes.
TA is an excellent hero to learn Tread switching on since she can make use of all three attributes and frequently gets a Bottle.

counters.text: If you apply "overkill" damage onto a layer of TA's Refraction barrier, it won't start cutting into the next layer. Any single damage instance beyond removing a layer to 0 will be ignored.
notes: For example, if you Lion Finger of Death a TA's Refraction barrier, you'll only remove one layer of her barrier.

Damage over time spells are a convenient way to add damage instances that can help tick a Refraction barrier past 0 to start using the next layer. Batrider, Jakiro, Phoenix, Venomancer, and Viper are examples of heroes with spells that are handy at clearing off Refraction.
Items that apply damage over time like Blood Grenade, Urn/Vessel/Distiller, and Radiance can also slowly help tick Refraction barriers past 0.
Illusion heroes (like Naga Siren, Phantom Lancer, and Terrorblade) are good at dealing with Refraction since each illusion's attack could remove a Refraction layer.

counters.text: You can't break TA's Meld with any stun or silence since Meld invisibility is an infinite duration undispellable buff, not a channeled spell. Your team really needs to have ground targeted spells or detection (Dust or sentry wards), otherwise she'll just sit there until her Blink comes off cooldown.
notes: However, spells that change her horizontal position with forced movement or knockback like Batrider's Flamebreak, Clockwerk's Power Cogs, Dark Seer's Vacuum, Drow Ranger's Gust, Invoker's Deafening Blast, Keeper of the Light's Blinding Light, Magnus's Skewer, Mars's Spear, Primal Beast's Onslaught, Queen of Pain's Sonic Wave, Spirit Breaker's Charge, or Void Spirit's Aether Remnant can break Meld by moving her.

counters.text: Essence Distiller can provide true sight on the debuffed target, such as Templar Assassin in Meld.
Know what you're getting yourself into if you dive a TA. Can you handle her having Refraction? Do you have detection if she Melds? Will you be able to kill her if she has five Traps lying around?
Always be moving around when you're against her mid. Make her miss last hits because she's too busy trying to Psi Blade spill on you.
If you activate Glyph, Psi Blades can't spill any damage off of your creeps. Could be handy to know in a low HP mid lane skirmish situation.

If you're mid against Lanaya, get some sentry wards at around 5 minutes. Not only will this allow you to actually finish a gank on her if you get the upper hand and she tries to hide with Meld, but you can also clear the Trap(s) that you know she has on your side of the hill.
notes: If you have a spell that she can disjoint in the laning phase with Meld invisibility, it can be worth getting a sentry ward even earlier.

counters.text: Smokes are great against teams with a TA since they will often be lazy when spamming observer wards if they can rely on Trap vision. On the other hand, you need to be careful that you're not Smoking on top of a Trap.

Traps don't give vision if placed inside the Rosh pit, but she may have seen your team walking into the pit with a Trap in front of the pit entrance. All the more reason to Smoke into the pit when against a TA.
notes: Runes are also very commonly Trapped by TA, so she may see you if you're camping the rune before it spawns.

tips.text: Terrorblade's Dark Unity innate changes how much damage your illusions do depending on how far they are from your hero.
notes: Reflection illusions are also affected.

tips.text: Reflection works on heroes that are in fog, but not invisible heroes.

Reflection illusions carry all the auras that normal illusions carry. It's quite useful to cast Reflection on heroes with aura items (like Radiance, Shiva's Guard, or Assault Cuirass) or aura passives (like Beastmaster's Inner Beast, Drow Ranger's Precision Aura, Lycan's Feral Impulse, or Vengeful Spirit's Vengeance Aura).

Reflection illusions don't consider Terrorblade to be the damage source, so you don't need to worry about Reflection illusions damaging an enemy Blade Mail or Nyx Assassin's Spiked Carapace and reflecting onto your main hero.
Use Conjure Image illusions to stack the jungle, serve as wards, intercept an incoming creep wave, or deny runes in the early game.
Terrorblade illusions can only be in Metamorphosis form if the real hero is within 1200 range of them.

If you create an illusion on the exact same tick that Metamorphosis times out on your hero, the illusion will spawn in Metamorphosis form for its entire duration. This works with Conjure Image and Manta Style illusions, but is not easy to pull off consistently.

Each Conjure Image cast spawns the illusion in a counterclockwise fashion around your hero. Spawns will rotate between north of your hero, west of your hero, then south, then east, and repeat. Not particularly useful, but it is cool trivia.
Be aware that basic illusions (like from Conjure Image) have a fixed 800/400 day/night vision which is significantly less than a hero's base vision.
Sunder can be cast on allies and illusions (like Conjure Image or Manta Style illusions).
You can't Sunder debuff immune/BKB'd enemies or allies.
Sunder has a minimum HP transfer percentage. If you and a target are both below the percentage, Sunder will heal you both to the minimum.
If you use Sunder while in a "wraith" form, like from Wraith King's Agh's Scepter, you will Sunder the target as if you have 1 HP.

You can Sunder through Ancient Apparition's Ice Blast to gain HP. You can Sunder a Borrowed Time Abaddon to make him lose HP. Sunder is considered an HP swap; it doesn't behave as a traditional source of damage/heal.
Infused Raindrops can be super value on TB. He has tons of armor, but is very susceptible to magic damage nukes.
There is a brief delay when activating Agh's Scepter Terror Wave before the fear actually goes out.
Agh's Scepter Terror Wave will follow your hero as you move similar to a Shiva's Guard active.

counters.text: The Reflection slow and illusion can be removed with basic dispels.
Reflection illusions carry all things that normal illusions carry. This includes item auras, so be wary about building things like Radiance or Assault Cuirass against a TB.

TB has armor for days, but very little HP to back it up. Magic damage makes life for TB and his illusions hell. If your team is mostly physical damage, consider building Maelstrom or Shiva's (yeah I know I just told you not to build auras, but Shiva's is usually worth it) to clear his illusions.
Sunder. It's a spell. That swaps your HP for his. Something you should be acutely aware of when trying to kill him.
Any level of Dagon can instakill illusions. As do spells like Disruptor's Glimpse, Pudge's Meat Hook, Skywrath Mage's Mystic Flare, and any Hex.
notes: Brewmaster's Storm Brewling with Dispel Magic deals full damage to all types of illusions.

counters.text: Dazzle's Poison Touch when cast from his Nothl Projection applies a hex to all units hit. This is a useful tool for mass clearing illusions.
Enchantress can take control of enemy illusions with Enchant.

Illusions your team creates of an enemy Terrorblade will spawn in Metamorphosis form if the hero himself has it activated, but they won't transform if TB activates Meta afterwards. The transformation only works on illusions Terrorblade owns.
If you're a carry, consider buying a Revenant's Brooch to bypass Terrorblade's extremely high armor in the late game.
The Agh's Scepter Terror Wave fear can be dispelled by basic dispels.

tips.text: Mechanically, think of Avalanche as being similar to a mini Faceless Void Chronosphere. The Avalanche AoE is an aura that is constantly stunning. So throw it in advance if you know a hero will be in the AoE before it finishes (mid-banish, pre-TP).
notes: This also means that strong dispels, like from Abaddon's Aphotic Shield or Slark's Dark Pact, can't remove Avalanche's stun debuff.
Avalanche is also unaffected by status resistance.

tips.text: Toss fully disables the thrown unit (allies and enemies). It counts as a stun, so stagger it after Avalanche ends on an enemy to maximize disable time.
notes: Tossing enemy or allied heroes will break their channels.

tips.text: Debuff immune/BKB'd targets can never be thrown as a Tossed unit.
Toss damages enemy buildings if a unit lands near it.
notes: With Agh's Shard, Toss will even slow enemy tower attack speed if a unit lands near it.

tips.text: You can Toss people to runes.
Toss always grabs the unit closest to Tiny.
Targeting Toss on an enemy hero will pop their Linken's Sphere, but you can still grab a Linken's Sphere'd enemy and Toss them to something else.
notes: If you target Toss's landing on to an enemy that has Lotus Orb, they will Toss whatever you threw at them right back to you.

tips.text: While you do need vision of a Toss target, you don't need vision of the unit you're going to Toss. Say an enemy is juking in fog, you can just mash Toss on a nearby target and Tiny will immediately grab the nearest valid unit, even if they're in fog, and Toss them. Useful against something like a Tree Dancing Monkey King who you can't see.
notes: You can't Toss invisible units, though. So to clarify: You can Toss units that aren't visible, but you can't Toss units that are in visible. Got it? Good.

tips.text: When you're getting ganked by melee enemies, always be looking for units to Toss your aggressors away to.
notes: Next level plays when playing against any melee range Blink initiation: Bait yourself by hanging around in enemy vision and start mashing Toss on a target nearby. The moment you get Blinked on, you'll immediately Toss the enemy before they can react. Toss has an instant cast animation, so you should theoretically be able to beat any kind of Blink initiation. This could be useful against heroes like Batrider or Magnus who have to get within Toss range to initiate on you.

tips.text: If allies are caught on the edge of a Faceless Void Chronosphere, you can Toss them out.
You can Toss targets in or out of a Disruptor's Kinetic Field.
notes: With BKB, you can potentially go into a Static Storm+Kinetic Field and Toss allies out to save them.

tips.text: You can Toss an ally straight up in the air and it'll count as enough distance to cancel Ancient Apparition's Cold Feet even though it's z-axis distance.
Attacking a building with a Tree can splash/cleave damage onto creeps, but attacking creeps will not splash damage onto buildings.

When ground targeting a Tree Throw, the tree will disintegrate and damage the first enemy unit it collides into, ignoring structures. A Thrown Tree will not 'cleave,' but instead explode in a circular AoE around the target.
Throwing a Tree provides vision as it travels.

Tree Throw's damage is applied as an instant attack on the target hit. This instant attack ignores disarms, has true strike, and applies attack modifiers. If you have an attack modifier with a proc, it'll roll for a chance to proc on the primary target.
notes: Since Tree Throw is an instant attack, it'll break your Smoke if it damages a unit.
You can activate Shadow Blade/Silver Edge after the Tree is thrown to get the backstab damage on the target hit.
The splash damage from a Thrown Tree is not classed as an instant attack. So you can't apply Desolator on everyone hit by a Thrown Tree, for example, only the primary target.

tips.text: You can't directly target couriers with Tree Throw, but a skillshotted Tree or a Throw that explodes near a courier can kill the donkey.
Denial attacks with a Tree will consume charges but won't cleave onto enemies.

Let your right clicks finish. Tiny's attack speed is constantly changing throughout the course of the game, which makes it a real pain to consistently cancel his backswing animation. Err on the side of caution and be patient.

You can "store" the max attack speed second hit of an Echo Sabre/Harpoon by canceling the attack before it connects. The attack speed buff lasts indefinitely, so you can spend the first right click on a creep and then store the fast attack for another target.
Echo Sabre/Harpoon will apply the slow with every Agh's Scepter Tree Volley attack and not go on cooldown.
Agh's Scepter Tree Volley trees benefit from Agh's Shard Tree Throw buffs.

counters.text: As long as the rocks are flying around, an Avalanche will stun you if you walk into the AoE.
Avalanche completely ignores any sources of status resistance.
Avalanche's stun can't be removed with strong dispels (like Abaddon's Aphotic Shield) because it's an aura, similar to a Faceless Void's Chronosphere.
Beware of being Tossed backwards into Tiny's tower during the laning phase. If Tiny starts running towards you for no good reason, watch out.
Breaks don't disable any aspect of Tiny's Grow. Would be pretty funny if it did, though.
notes: Breaks do disable his Insurmountable innate, however.

counters.text: Tiny is all about burst comboing enemies down. Consider investing in HP items (Blood Grenade, Fluffy Hat, Bracer) if you're a squishy support that keeps getting one-shotted.
